description:
## Background

Graph can now show Focused and complete relationship maps, but users cannot inspect an Issue without returning to List mode. The product contract calls for the existing Issue Detail presentation in a nonmodal panel over the right side of the canvas. Selection is real Issue Navigation state, not private component state.

This work depends on both the reusable Issue Detail prefactor and the complete graph/scope foundation.

Triage: ready-for-agent.

## What to build

Let users activate a Graph card to open Issue Detail over the canvas, close the overlay to an unselected Graph entry, and use Back/Forward to restore selection and scope.

## Technical Approach

- Support `/graph/<issue-id>` and `/graph/<issue-id>?scope=all` as selected Graph destinations.
- Make mouse and keyboard card activation push a selected Graph navigation entry while retaining the current scope.
- Resolve selected detail from the successful `allIssues` snapshot, not only the visible card collection.
- Render the extracted Issue Detail presentation in a nonmodal panel over the right side of the canvas.
- Keep the canvas interactive while the panel is open.
- Ensure the selected Issue is a Focused seed so a closed selected Issue remains visible.
- Keep or pan the selected card into the canvas area not covered by the overlay without changing its computed graph position.
- Closing the panel pushes an unselected Graph entry with the same scope. It does not call browser Back.
- Back after Close reopens the prior selected Graph entry; Forward closes it again.
- Reuse the existing Issue-not-found presentation when a selected Graph route does not resolve.
- Keep copied external Issue links view-agnostic so they continue opening normal List detail.

## Considerations

- Following Issue References within the overlay is explicitly the next child. This slice covers card selection, inspection, Close, and browser history.
- Do not create a Graph-specific detail view model or duplicate Markdown, metadata, comments, Child Issues, or copy-deep-link behavior.
- Scope changes while detail is open should preserve the selected Issue.
- The overlay must not trap canvas interaction as a modal would.
- Viewport persistence across navigation and refresh is a later child; this issue only prevents immediate overlay occlusion of the selected card.
- The route remains authoritative when the Issue is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pointer and keyboard activation of a card push a selected Graph navigation entry.
- [ ] Selected Graph routes preserve Focused or Show-all scope.
- [ ] The reused Issue Detail renders in a right-side nonmodal overlay without duplicating its presentation logic.
- [ ] The selected card stays visible in the uncovered canvas area while the overlay is open.
- [ ] A selected closed Issue remains a visible Focused seed.
- [ ] Close pushes an unselected Graph entry with the same scope.
- [ ] Back after Close reopens the selected overlay and Forward closes it again.
- [ ] A missing selected Issue shows the existing not-found presentation while retaining the route.
- [ ] External copied Issue links remain view-agnostic.
- [ ] `mise run doctor:react` and `mise run verify` pass.

## Test Plan

- Route/history tests for selected Focused and Show-all entries, Close push semantics, Back, and Forward.
- Graph component tests for pointer and keyboard card activation, overlay rendering, canvas usability, selected-card visibility, and missing Issue.
- Reusable Issue Detail regression tests prove the Graph overlay uses the same Markdown, metadata, comments, Child Issues, and copy action.
- App integration tests cover switching List → selected Graph and Graph → List without losing the selected Issue.
- Run the canonical `mise run verify` gate.
title: Open and close Issue Detail over Graph
